text.lead: Salvation Army is a 2013 French-Swiss-Moroccan drama film written and directed by Abdellah Taia in his directorial debut. It is an adaptation of Taia's 2006 autobiographical novel of the same name. Taia submitted the controversial film's original screenplay to the National Centre for Moroccan Cinema, hoping it would be released in Morocco. The film won multiple awards and was screened at the Venice Film Festival.
text.plot: The film follows Abdellah, a young Moroccan gay man with a distant father, a demanding mother, and an older brother he looks up to. Abdellah is trying to find his way in a society that denies his sexuality. Once he leaves to college in Geneva, he finds freedom but must come to terms with the loss of his homeland.
